title: Routing decision explainability: instrumentation, compact decision logs, and per-hop metrics
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Add a focused instrumentation layer and compact decision-log schema to make routing decisions auditable, explainable, and queryable by SREs and platform teams. This ticket covers the telemetry schema design, sampling and retention strategy, ingest/aggregation flow, and Console integration for per-hop metrics and a concise human-readable "explain" view for requests that flow through policy routing (region selection, tier routing, and fallback model variants).

Motivation: Operators and PMs need to validate that policy routing behaves as intended under load and during degradations. Current observability provides traces and some route metrics, but there is no compact, queryable decision record that ties: policy inputs (region, tier, model variants), the decision score or priority that chose a path, per-hop latency/cost contribution, and the fallback reason when one occurred. This gap makes debugging regressions and customer incidents slow and error prone.

Non-goals: This ticket is not adding new routing policies or changing decision logic. It also does not implement long-term archival storage beyond configurable retention tiers (we'll store full payloads in cold storage via downstream jobs).
acceptance_criteria: A compact decision-log event (JSONL) is emitted for 100% of requests in debug-sampled mode and for 1% of production requests by default.

Decision log includes: request_id, correlation_ids, timestamp, policy_inputs (region_hint, customer_tier, model_family), chosen_path, decision_score, fallback_reason (if any), per-hop latency_ms, per-hop token_cost_estimate, node_id and model_variant_id.
OTel trace links: each decision log includes trace_id and span_id allowing correlation to distributed traces in Jaeger/Tempo.
Console: a new "Routing Explain" panel in the Request Details view that renders the decision-log in readable form and highlights fallback occurrences and top latency contributors.
Per-hop aggregated metrics (p50/p95 latency, token_cost) available in Metrics backend and surfaced in the Console route-level dashboard.
Logging and storage follow PII-minimization rules: no user prompt text is included in the decision log; only prompt length/token_count is allowed.
Automated e2e test that verifies a forced fallback path emits a decision log with fallback_reason and a retriable flag set to true.
telemetry_schema: fields: request_id, trace_id, span_id, timestamp_iso, customer_id_hash, region_hint, chosen_region, customer_tier, policy_version, model_family, model_variant_id, decision_score, fallback_reason, per_hop:[hop_index, node_id, op_type, latency_ms, token_cost_estimate], total_latency_ms, total_token_cost_estimate, sampling_rate
compact_encoding: JSONL line, max 12kb uncompressed for debug events
implementation_notes: Emit decision events synchronously to the local log writer with backpressure bypass: if telemetry queue is full, increment a telemetry_drop counter and continue request path (no request blocking).

Use OTLP/gRPC exporter for bulk ingestion into the telemetry pipeline. Events should be tagged with telemetry_dataset=routing_decision and routed to a short-term hot index for fast queries and a cold store for longer retention.
Implement a compact serializer in runtime (C++) that minifies keys and applies field dictionaries for common values (e.g., model_family -> codes) to keep debug events size-bounded.
Add feature flag `routing_decision_debug` to enable 100% sampling for a given request_id prefix (used by SE/support).
Ensure privacy: redact any free-text fields; include token_count instead of prompt content. Run security review checklist if future additions include user data.
tasks: Runtime instrumentation: emit decision logs and per-hop timing (ENG)
Ingest pipeline mapping: OTLP collector config and hot index mapping (Infra)
Metrics aggregation job: compute per-route p50/p95 per-hop token_cost and latency (Batch team)
Console UI: Routing Explain panel + per-hop breakdown chart (Console UI)
E2E tests and load test to measure telemetry overhead (SRE)
Docs: PRD + runbook and sample queries for SREs and Support
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable debug sampling 100% for internal traffic in prod region-us-east and collect 48h of events; verify size and ingestion stability.
Phase 2 (limited): enable 1% rate sampling for all customers; expose Console panel to internal users only.
Phase 3 (GA): expose sampling toggle in Console per-org, increase retention options; enable route-level aggregated metrics in dashboards.
Rollback: disable sampling at ingestion layer and turn off Console panel visibility.
risks_and_mitigations: Telemetry overhead: compact serializer + sampling limits to bound ingestion costs; early load tests to validate.
Privacy leak risk: enforce schema linter in CI that rejects any field named 'prompt' or 'user_text' in decision events.
Operational churn: add dashboards to show telemetry pipeline saturation and set alerts on telemetry_drop rate.
notes: Related work: ties into SmartRouting policy metrics; this ticket intentionally focuses on observability rather than policy changes.
We should align model_family and model_variant identifiers with model catalog canonical IDs to simplify joins in analytics.
Consider a future compact binary protobuf encoding if JSONL becomes a bottleneck for debug traces.
